posts.content:
UniversalVault is a macOS menu-bar app that stores structured personal records encrypted on this Mac. Control+Option+V opens a search palette over whatever app you are in; search a field, press Return, and the value is typed into the focused field. An item can be marked protected, which seals its fields under a second key and asks for Touch ID before they are read. An item can also be marked for agents, which lets a local command print its non-sensitive fields as JSON. The vault opens at launch without a prompt. Sleep, screen lock, or an inactivity timeout close protected items only; Vault > Lock closes everything. There is no cloud sync.

Use it through a working day: fill a few forms in other apps, add an item, protect one, come back after lunch, and look something up again. Describe what happened, what you expected to happen, what you tried next, and what it cost you in time, attention, or trust.

comments.content: I tested this as a bookkeeper who lives in spreadsheets, not code. I filled three vendor forms in other apps using the Control+Option+V palette, then added a client record, protected it, and went to lunch. Coming back: the protected item asked for Touch ID as described, and unlocking was quick. The important part for me is record consistency, so I tried to undo a field edit, duplicate an item, and delete the duplicate. I could not tell from the description whether an edit is undoable or whether deleting an item is truly reversible, and I did not see how duplicate detection works. I also noticed the item list can reorder itself depending on recent use, which makes me nervous when I am reconciling four hundred records; I would want a stable sort and a visible indication of what changed and when. My search expectation is that the palette searches every field I can see, including custom field names I invented, not just the standard ones. On accessibility, the palette text needs to respect larger system text sizing. On privacy, no cloud sync is good, but “opens at launch without a prompt” means anything not marked protected is readable to anyone at the unlocked Mac. For non-sensitive fields printed by a local agent, I would want a very clear boundary and an audit line showing which command read which item and when. What did the undo/duplicate/delete tests cost me? About ten minutes of hesitating before trusting the delete, and I would not store client data until I know whether the list order and the search scope are predictable.

Leo esto con el Mac de casa delante, que lo comparto con mi hijo adolescente, y hay dos cosas que me dejan intranquila. La primera: "la bóveda se abre al arrancar sin pedir nada". Yo siempre he dado por hecho que con cerrar sesión en el Mac ya quedaba todo a salvo, y por lo que cuentas eso no es así: para cerrarlo TODO hay que entrar en Vault > Lock a mano, y dormir la pantalla o bloquear solo cierra lo protegido. La segunda: lo de marcar un elemento "para agentes" y que un comando imprima campos en JSON. Para quien no vivimos en el Mac, eso suena a otra puerta abierta, aunque digas que son campos no sensibles. ¿Podrías explicar cómo se ve en el día a día sin saber de terminal, y qué pasa si alguien de la casa borra un registro sin querer? Yo tiendo a cerrar las apps en vez de bloquearlas y siempre pienso que lo borrado ya no está, así que necesito saber si hay forma de recuperarlo y cuánto cuesta tener esto bajo control.
